questions.question: Which letters does the musical alphabet use?
options: C to B, with no A
questions.explanation: Seven letters, A B C D E F G. After G it starts again at A, an octave higher.

questions.question: How far does the note move when you go up one fret?
questions.explanation: One fret is always a half step, on every string. Two frets make a whole step.

questions.question: Which two pairs of letters have no note between them?
questions.explanation: B to C and E to F are only one fret apart. Every other pair of letters is two frets apart, with a sharp or flat between.

questions.question: What are the open strings, from thickest to thinnest?
options: E B G D A E
E A D G B E
E A D G C F
A D G C E A
questions.explanation: E A D G B E. Eddie Ate Dynamite, Good Bye Eddie.

questions.question: What note is at fret 5 on the low E string?
questions.explanation: E, F (fret 1), G (fret 3), A (fret 5). It is also the open A string, the next string up.

questions.question: Where is C on the A string?
questions.explanation: A, then B at fret 2, then C one fret later at fret 3, because B to C is a half step.

questions.question: What happens at fret 12?
options: Every string plays its open note again, an octave higher
Each string plays the note of the next string
questions.explanation: Twelve half steps make an octave, so fret 12 repeats the open strings an octave up, and the pattern starts over.

questions.question: F♯ and G♭ are…
options: Two different notes a half step apart
The same note with two names
Only found on the high e string
questions.explanation: Both names point to the same fret. F raised by a half step and G lowered by a half step land in the same place.

questions.question: G is at fret 3 on the low E string. Where is the G one octave higher, two strings up?
questions.explanation: From the low E or A string, the octave is two strings up and two frets higher: fret 5 on the D string.
